zh.question: 同样是岩浆，为什么有时流出来，有时会猛烈喷出碎屑？
zh.observe: 固定喷口数量，分别降低和提高气体、黏度条件；推进同一阶段，比较流动与碎屑。再增加喷口，追踪地下到地表的连接。

academic.title: 岩浆上升时气体会发生变化
academic.body: 岩浆是包含熔融物、晶体和气体的体系，不是地球内部到处存在的一片液态海洋。上升过程中围压降低，原先溶在熔体中的部分挥发组分可析出并形成气泡。气泡膨胀、上升、聚合与逸出共同影响喷发；有气体不代表必然爆炸，关键还包括释放气体的速度和通道是否通畅。

academic.title: 黏度与气体逸出相互影响
academic.body: 温度、成分和晶体含量都会影响岩浆的流变性质。较高黏度通常使气泡逸出更困难，在一些条件下有利于压力积累和碎裂；流动较容易、气体较易逸出的岩浆常出现溢流。但真实喷发还受供浆速度、外来水和通道演化影响，不能把两根滑块当成完整分类器。

academic.title: 喷口形态与喷出物都要辨认
academic.body: 岩浆到达地表后称为熔岩，可从中央喷口或裂隙流出。爆炸性喷发的火山灰是细碎的岩石、矿物和火山玻璃，并不是燃烧留下的普通灰烬。火山气体、落灰、熔岩流和火山碎屑密度流具有不同危险机制；画面只表现部分过程，不能由熔岩流得慢就推断整座火山安全。

zh.misconception: 火山不是地下有火在烧；火山灰也不是木头烧完的灰。
zh.boundary: 这是相对条件示意，未计算温度、压力、喷发柱或危险距离；观察真实火山须遵守当地封闭和预警。

narration.label: 山下面有什么
narration.text: 看到火山喷出红亮的东西，你会不会以为山下面点着一堆火？其实那是很热的岩浆，里面有熔化的岩石成分，也可能有晶体和气体。它不是燃烧的木柴。我们从剖面开始，看看地下的岩浆，怎样沿着通道向上移动。
narration.cue: 停在地下剖面，指向通道。

narration.label: 气泡长大了
narration.text: 当岩浆来到更靠近地面的地方，周围压着它的力量常常变小，里面的一些气体就会形成气泡，气泡还会膨胀。有时气体比较容易出去，有时却没那么顺利。先慢慢推进，看看气泡和岩浆往哪里走，再猜猜改变条件会发生什么。
narration.cue: 推进减压与气泡阶段，留三秒预测。

narration.label: 流动，或者喷出碎片
narration.text: 现在把岩浆容易流动的程度和气体条件换一换。你看到了比较平缓的流出，还是更明显的碎片喷出？岩浆到地面上，我们叫它熔岩。细细的火山灰则是岩石和玻璃一类的小碎片。它们虽然叫灰，却不是篝火留下的灰。
narration.cue: 对照低高黏度及气体条件。

narration.label: 模型帮助提问
narration.text: 再增加几个喷口，找找它们怎样和地下连接。真正的火山比这幅图复杂得多，科学家会一起观察地面变化、地震和气体。我们的小模型能帮助问为什么，不能告诉我们哪里安全。如果去火山地区，一定跟着大人遵守警示，不靠近喷口和新鲜熔岩。

en.question: Why can magma sometimes flow out and sometimes erupt explosively as fragments?
en.observe: Keep vent count fixed and compare low and high gas and viscosity at the same stage. Then add vents and trace their connection from below ground to the surface.

academic.title: Gas changes as magma rises
academic.body: Magma contains melt, crystals and gas; Earth is not filled with a universal underground liquid ocean. Falling pressure during ascent allows dissolved volatile components to form bubbles. Their expansion, coalescence and escape influence eruption behavior. Gas presence alone does not guarantee an explosion; escape rate and connected pathways matter.

academic.title: Viscosity interacts with gas escape
academic.body: Composition, temperature and crystal content affect magma flow. Higher viscosity can hinder gas escape and, under some conditions, promote pressure buildup and fragmentation. Easier flow and gas release often accompany effusion. Supply rate, external water and evolving conduits also influence real eruptions.

academic.title: Identify vents and eruption products
academic.body: Magma at the surface is lava and may emerge from central vents or fissures. Volcanic ash consists of fine rock, mineral and volcanic-glass fragments, not ordinary combustion ash. Gases, ashfall, lava and pyroclastic density currents pose different hazards; slowly moving lava does not make a volcano safe.

en.misconception: A volcano is not an underground fire, and volcanic ash is not burnt wood ash.
en.boundary: This comparison does not calculate temperature, pressure, eruption columns or safe distances. Follow local closures and warnings near real volcanoes.

narration.label: What is under the mountain?
narration.text: A volcano may release glowing red material, but that does not mean someone lit a fire under the mountain. Very hot magma contains melted rock material and may contain crystals and gas. It is not burning wood. Begin with the cutaway and follow the route by which magma can move upward.
narration.cue: Hold the underground cutaway and point to the conduit.

narration.label: Bubbles grow
narration.text: As magma approaches the surface, the surrounding pressure often falls. Some of its dissolved gas can form bubbles, and those bubbles expand. Sometimes gas escapes readily; sometimes it cannot. Move forward slowly and watch where bubbles and magma go before predicting what a change in conditions might do.
narration.cue: Advance decompression and bubbles, then pause for three seconds.

narration.label: Flow or fragments
narration.text: Change how easily the magma flows and the gas conditions. Do you see more flowing material or more fragments being expelled? Magma at the surface is called lava. Fine volcanic ash is made of little pieces of rock and volcanic glass. Despite its name, it is different from ash left by a campfire.
narration.cue: Compare low and high viscosity and gas conditions.

narration.label: A model helps us ask
narration.text: Add vents and look for their underground connections. Real volcanoes are much more complex. Scientists observe ground movement, earthquakes and gas together. Our model helps us ask why, but cannot tell us where it is safe. In volcanic areas, follow warnings with an adult and stay away from vents and fresh lava.
narration.cue: Add vents, then return to the overview.
